newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty genl wins court order in tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty genl wins court order in tobacco case.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said Thursday he won a court order directing the Liggett Group to turn over documents.
Liggett, the fifth-largest U.S. tobacco business, is owned by Brooke Group Ltd.

Liggett filed five boxes of documents under seal in superior court in Litchfield, Conn., where the state's case against the tobacco companies is being heard, Blumenthal said in a statement. Judge Michael Sheldon also directed the companies to explain by April 4 why all the documents should not be disclosed to Blumenthal.
The judge also rejected the companies' effort to have a North Carolina judge prevent the documents from being filed in the Connecticut court.
Connecticut filed its $1 billion lawsuit against tobacco companies last July, seeking reimbursement for state expenses for tobacco-related diseases and other penalties.
Connecticut was the tenth of 22 state that have sued tobacco companies.
The lawsuit claims that tobacco companies hook children into tobacco use through targeted advertising and promotions and manipulate nicotine levels to create and maintain addiction to their products.
"Incredibly, the industry sought a court order in North Carolina to suppress these documents without notice to the states and without their knowledge or participation," Blumenthal said.
"Clearly, the burden should be on the defendants to explain why the documents produced by Liggett should be hidden from the state."
